title: LINQ translation server client evaluation and IQueryable
concepts: An EF LINQ query begins as an expression tree rooted in a provider-backed IQueryable. Operators compose a query description until a terminal operator or enumeration executes it.

The provider translates the expression to database-specific commands. Not every .NET method or comparer can be translated; unsupported expressions inside filters generally fail rather than silently loading the whole table.

Client evaluation is explicit when crossing to IEnumerable or asynchronous enumeration, and is permitted in the final projection for some expressions. Materialize only after server-side filtering and projection have reduced data.

Terminal operators differ in cardinality expectations: First, Single, Any, and Count each express a different result contract. Async variants allow nonblocking I/O but do not make a DbContext safe for concurrent operations.
ToQueryString and logging help inspect translation, but generated SQL and provider behavior must be tested against the real database engine.

versionNotes.edition: EF Core 11.0.0 released 2026-11-10; LINQ translations checked 2026-11-16
items: EF Core 10.0 is an LTS release and supports .NET 10 LeftJoin and RightJoin translation. EF Core 11.0.0 shipped 2026-11-10 and supports .NET 11 FullJoin translation, MaxBy/MinBy translation, GroupBy enhancements, removal of redundant joins/order keys, and no-op cast stripping. The Microsoft EF11 What's New page retains a stale development banner; use the final .NET 11 release notes for release status. Provider translation remains provider-specific.
